recommendation: Keep this audit as-is. Reconcile future resource-local intent comments under their specific resource Jira issues rather than duplicating or broadening FHIR-15686's Request-pattern change.
issue_request: FHIR-15686 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-I and asked the Request pattern to make clear that intent is immutable: a proposal should not turn into an order on the same instance, and a separate Request with a different intent should be created using Request.basedOn.
initial_application: No source commit naming FHIR-15686 was found. Historical commit 14b69a1c6dd33918b20d53ffd6cfbab523f840ba appears to have applied the issue by adding '(immutable)' and the current Request.intent comment to source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists request under [logical], making the Request spreadsheet current build-scope source. Later FHIR-20607 Request-pattern work clarified related narrative without changing the intent rule, while resource-specific follow-ups such as FHIR-20606 and FHIR-20605 govern local CarePlan and MedicationRequest wording.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no source change is needed: source/request/request-spreadsheet.xml already contains the immutable-intent rule, the new basedOn instance instruction, and the Request.intent granularity exception.

related_jiras.note: Clarified Request narrative around immutable terminology and same-intent replacements without superseding the FHIR-15686 Request.intent rule.
Applied the same immutable-intent comment to CarePlan.intent and noted CarePlan does not need the Request.intent granularity exception.
MedicationRequest-specific intent guidance confirms the Request pattern granularity exception remains relevant for hierarchical request intent codes.
